build_inputs.angles:
1. Lead on this: 564 horsepower, all-wheel drive and 360 miles of range, for less than people pay for a used Camry. Open on the numbers and on how little the money is. Do not name the make or the model in the first sentence, and do not mention that the company is dead yet - that reveal belongs in the next beat, because withholding it is what makes it land.

2. Then the reveal and the history, in that order: name the car, then say the company that built it went bankrupt. Then the part that is funny because it is simply true - Fisker cut this exact trim from about 69,000 dollars to about 61,500 in October 2023, then to about 37,500 in March 2024, and filed for Chapter 11 anyway in June 2024. They nearly halved the price and still could not sell them. Production stopped in March 2024 after roughly 11,200 cars. Verify every one of those figures.

3. Cover the catch and play it completely straight, because deadpan is what makes this funny and a joke would kill it. There is no manufacturer behind the car. Software updates now come from a volunteer owner community instead of the factory. The leftover factory stock, about 3,300 cars, went to a single leasing company for roughly 14,000 dollars each, and a lot of them now run Uber trips in Manhattan. Owners have wired reset switches into the cabin fuse box so they can reboot the car when the screen freezes. State all of that flatly and do not editorialise - the facts are the punchline and commentary would flatten them.

4. Cover what the money buys, because the equipment list is absurd next to the price: dual motors, a 113 kilowatt-hour battery, a solar panel built into the roof, and a 17-inch screen that physically rotates. Do not claim a figure for what the solar roof generates unless it can be verified.

5. Say once, early and in a single clause, that this is a run on cheap electric cars whose makers no longer exist. Do not spend a beat on it.

6. Close on the question and keep it light: would you flex 564 horsepower that nobody on earth can service, or is this the worst bargain ever built?

script: 564 horsepower, all-wheel drive and up to 360 miles of range for less than a used Toyota Camry: they go for about $16,000 today. That's the 2023 Fisker Ocean One, the Extreme's launch edition, and Fisker filed for Chapter 11 in June 2024 after building roughly 11,200 Oceans. The Extreme, not the One, dropped from about $69,000 to $61,000 in October 2023, then $37,000 in March 2024. Production stopped that March - that's before Fisker's June bankruptcy filing. Dual motors draw from a 113-kilowatt-hour battery and deliver 543 pound-feet of torque when you engage Boost Mode. The Fisker Owners Association coordinates software updates through a network of volunteers and independent service partners. Factory support's now gone. The 17.1-inch touchscreen physically rotates for parked movie streaming, and you can still adjust climate settings without stopping playback. Would you risk orphaned electric muscle, or is this the worst bargain ever built?

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2023 Fisker Ocean One, finished in Mariana Metallic with a Black Abyss Plus interior. The odometer on this Ocean currently displays approximately 10,800 miles. This Fisker is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes a Hyper Range battery pack, 22-inch F3b SlipStream wheels, a SolarSky roof panel, and a Revolve 17.1-inch touchscreen. Notable modifications reported by the seller include a Fisker OS 2.6.1 software update, a CarLink kit for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and an aftermarket TPMS system. Built in Graz, Austria, the Ocean represents Fisker's latest attempt at merging into the automotive mainstream. It's an electric crossover that offers available all-wheel drive, space for five passengers, and a long list of tech features including a 17.1-inch touchscreen. Production ended in 2024. Power comes from two electric motors, which draw electricity from a 113-kilowatt-hour lithium-ion battery pack to power all four wheels with up to 564 horsepower and 543 lb-ft of torque with Boost Mode engaged. In 2023, the Ocean received a maximum driving range rating of 360 miles from the EPA when equipped with the Hyper Range battery.
